div.div: Only ONE box in the stack is a language model: perception, the engage trigger, the body and the gaze are plain code that unit tests can prove; the model's behaviour can only be measured live

MICROPHONE ARRAY
audio in

HEAD CAMERA
frames stay inside the stand

VISITOR PERCEPTION - not an LLM
small vision and audio models: face detector, face embedding (anonymous session id), active-speaker detection, voice embedding; direction-of-arrival fusion; state machine absent -> arming -> engaged

ENGAGE TRIGGER - not an LLM
one deterministic edge: 'engaged' -> one system message to greet. Cooldown, re-arm on idle, wake-word precedence, fail closed if perception is stale

THE REASONER - the only LLM
a realtime speech-to-speech session: audio in and out, server-side VAD, function calling; the only 'vision' is a camera frame per utterance.
Wrapped by: a local wake-word gate; TRIAGE (a per-utterance LLM decision: accept or ignore); a barge-in guard; context compaction; tracing.
Behaviour lives in prompt files: base identity and safety <- stand profile <- one file per ability

LOUDSPEAKER
robot voice out

BEHAVIOUR LIBRARY - not an LLM
a behaviour tree at 100 Hz [I1] with blended priority layers; face lights, eyebrows and a nod follow the voice output level

GAZE CONTROLLER - not an LLM
active-speaker bearing -> gaze policy -> head-pose command (diagram 05)

ROBOT GATEWAY - not an LLM
the only component that talks to the robot middleware; a few intent verbs: speak, play pose, look at, hand over, cancel, health
TWO DESIGNS IN THE SOURCES
on-rails (designed first)
speech-to-speech (as built)
where the LLM sits
inside one beat, fixed intents and output schema
the voice AND the sequencer
robustness in noise
high
lower
latency
near zero for canned lines
one model round trip
auditability
every line enumerable, testable in CI
not enumerable: safety is measured
charm
repetitive without pools
varied
Likely posture under crowd noise: a hybrid (canned openers, live follow-ups). A voice pack of pre-rendered lines is always the floor.
AUTOMATIC, FAIL-CLOSED AUDIO LADDER (each step down is more robust)
1 open microphone, full duplex (listens while speaking)
2 half duplex: microphone closed while the robot speaks
3 push-to-talk
4 canned lines + gestures driven by a hidden operator (Wizard-of-Oz floor): the visitor cannot tell
A cloud call is never awaited on the critical path: a stall falls back to a canned line from the beat's pool.

DESIGN INVARIANTS. Camera data stays inside the stand; only bearings, flags and actions cross to the robot. Visitor context enriches conversation, never control: mood may shape a line, never a state transition. A safety supervisor sits above the state machine and pre-empts any state. Free conversation stays off the gateway seam. The reasoner never returns to idle by itself: consumers infer 'conversation over', e.g. after 5 s of quiet listening [I2]. Exactly one publisher of the reasoner state.

Legend: purple, thick border = the one language model (and its prompt-owned behaviour) | blue = perception and trigger (plain code) | green = body and gaze | grey = sensors, speaker, gateway | purple arrows = model output, blue = perception output, green = motion commands.

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (a paper, standard or physics value, or my arithmetic on one); [In] = illustrative (a round design value of the right order; never a measurement of a real robot or visitor); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/B1-the-voice-pipeline.md (components as built, one visitor end to end, on-rails versus open conversation, reasoner as sequencer, degradation, design invariants, 'how it is designed and tested'); Wizard-of-Oz after Kelley 1984; cascade and speech-to-speech designs after Skantze 2021 (both cited in B1).
[I1] behaviour_tick_illustrative = 100 Hz. illustrative behaviour-library update rate
[I2] wind_down_quiet_illustrative = 5 s. illustrative quiet-listening time after which a supervisor infers 'conversation over'
